---
title: "Backends"
guide-section: "Reference"
---

One section per backend: the extra that installs it, its tier and flags, the
locator fields it reads (`tether add` options, `--set`, `Repo.add`), its
`[backends.<kind>]` config, what it records as state, how pins and forks map
onto the system, the handle `open` returns, and what `diff --content`
reports. Credentials are never stored in manifests.

| Kind | Extra | Maturity | Tier | Flags |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`file`](#file-local-paths-and-object-stores) | -- (local) / `objectstore` | stable | Observed; Addressable for a versioned remote object | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `DIFF`, `CREATE` (local directory) |
| [`icechunk`](#icechunk-icechunk-repositories) | `icechunk` | stable | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY`, `PROMOTE`, `CREATE` |
| [`git`](#git-git-and-jj-repositories) | -- | stable | Forkable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE`, `CREATE` |
| [`lance`](#lance-lance-datasets) | `lance` | stable | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY` |
| [`delta`](#delta-delta-lake-tables) | `delta` | stable | Addressable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY` |
| [`neon`](#neon-neon-postgres) | `neon` | experimental | Forkable | `NEEDS_QUIESCENCE`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `BRANCH_IS_STORAGE` |
| [`iceberg`](#iceberg-apache-iceberg-tables) | `iceberg` | experimental | Forkable | `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY`, `PROMOTE` |
| [`ducklake`](#ducklake-ducklake-catalogs) | `ducklake` | experimental | Addressable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `RETENTION_BOUND`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY` |
| [`dolt`](#dolt-dolt-databases) | `dolt` | experimental | Forkable | `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE` |
| [`memory`](#memory-in-process-reference-backend) | -- | stable | Forkable | `CHEAP_FINGERPRINT`, `ATOMIC_REF`, `DIFF`, `HISTORY`, `PROMOTE`, `MERGE`, `CREATE` (tests only) |

*Maturity* is what the backend declares (`MATURITY`; `tether backends` prints
it). **Stable** means the full lifecycle -- register, commit, fork, write,
commit, promote, gc -- runs in CI against the real system: embedded stores
and libraries, on local storage. The object-store paths of `file` and
`icechunk` (S3, GCS, Azure) have not run against a cloud service yet;
`ROADMAP.md` tracks that. **Experimental** is tested against a fake of a
network service and has not been run against the service itself by the
maintainers. `add` says so when you register an experimental kind. The tiers
and flags are defined in
[Writing a Backend](11-extending.qmd#capabilities-decide-behavior).

## Conventions

- `branch` in a locator is the *upstream* branch (default `main`): what the
  trunk bookmark stands for. On the trunk the working ref is that branch
  itself; on any other bookmark `tether new -b NAME` forks
  `tether.ws.<dataset8>.<bookmark>` from the pin.
- Pins are named `tether.<pin_id>` in the target system, where `pin_id` is
  `<dataset8>.<hash16>`: the dataset's id, then a content address of kind +
  identity + state. Backends treat the id as opaque; the engine keeps `gc`
  inside its own dataset's namespace.
- `identity` is the subset of the locator that names the system; two objects
  of one dataset with the same identity and state share one pin, and `commit`
  cuts it once: the second object is recorded at the state the pin was taken
  at, not at its own fingerprint of the same content (whose volatile address,
  a Neon LSN, may differ).
- Locators are committed and read from every directory and every clone, so a
  *relative* local path (`file` `uri`/`path`, `git` `path`,
  `icechunk`/`lance`/`delta` `uri`, `ducklake` `data_path` and the path in
  `metadata`, after `ducklake:`, `ducklake:duckdb:`, or `ducklake:sqlite:`) is resolved
  against the directory `add` or `import` ran in and stored absolute. URLs
  and absolute paths are stored as given.
- Objects that live in one *branch scope* -- two databases of a Neon
  project, two keys on one Icechunk store -- share a branch per bookmark:
  `new` forks it once and every member writes through it, and `gc` collects
  the pins every object references per scope before deciding what is
  unreferenced.
- `at` in a locator is an object's initial position (`tether add --at` /
  `--pick`): the first commit pins that native state instead of the `branch`
  head; a trunk `pull` later moves the object onto the branch. `tether log`
  lists what each system accepts:

| Kind | `at` accepts | `log` lists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icechunk` | snapshot id, tag, branch | `Repository.ancestry` from the ref: id, `written_at`, message |
| `lance` | version number (on the base branch) or tag | `versions()` of the branch, newest first, tags on each |
| `iceberg` | snapshot id or ref name | snapshot ancestry with operation and record counts |
| `delta` | version number | transaction log with operation and metrics |
| `ducklake` | snapshot id | `ducklake_snapshots` with each snapshot's changes |
| `dolt` | commit hash, tag, or branch (`HASHOF`) | `DOLT_LOG(ref)` |
| `git` | any commit-ish (alias of `ref`) | `git log` with decorations |
| `neon`, `file` | not supported | -- |

## What the flags mean in practice

**`PROMOTE` and `MERGE`.** `PROMOTE` means `tether promote` can fast-forward
the base branch to a fork (Icechunk `reset_branch`, Iceberg
`set-snapshot-ref`, git `merge --ff-only`, Dolt merges); `MERGE`
means it can three-way merge a diverged fork (git `merge`, `DOLT_MERGE`). Lance cannot move a branch head yet and Neon
cannot promote a child branch, so both are refused with instructions.

**`--pin record`** removes `PIN` from any backend: the state is recorded
without a native ref and `new` forks from it directly (Icechunk snapshot id,
Lance `(branch, version)`, Iceberg snapshot id, Dolt/git commit, Neon
LSN on the branch it was read from) for as long as the system still has that
state.

**`CREATE`** *(experimental)* is what `tether add --create` needs: the backend
can make an empty store, mark it as the dataset's, and remove it again once
`gc` finds nothing but tether's own refs in it (see
[Stores tether created](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#stores-tether-created)).
Lance, Delta, and Iceberg tables need a schema to exist and cannot be created
empty; Neon, Dolt, and DuckLake objects live inside a project,
database, or catalog tether does not own. For those kinds, make the store
with its own tools and `add` it.

## State keys: content and address

A state's keys do two jobs:

- **Content** keys say what the data is: an Icechunk snapshot id, a Neon
  `commit_xid`, a git sha. Equality (drift, `commit`'s unchanged check,
  `promote`), pin ids, and listing names use only these.
- **Address** keys say where to find or cut it and can move without the data
  changing: Neon's `lsn` advances on checkpoints; git's `change_id` exists only
  when jj is installed, and its `dirty` describes the checkout, not the
  commit. Backends list them in `VOLATILE_KEYS`; `open`, `pin`, and `verify`
  get the whole state.

Iceberg's `metadata_location`, which changes on every table commit on any
branch, is in neither: it is not part of the state at all.

## Content diffs

`tether diff A B` compares manifests: which objects were added, removed, or
changed (with pin ids). `--content` additionally asks each changed object's
backend for its *native* diff, using metadata only (no data is read), run
concurrently across objects:

| Kind | Unit | Source | Example detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` (dir / prefix) | files | two stored listings (`.tether/listings/`) | `modified a.tif +4.0 KiB` |
| `file` (object) | objects | recorded size / etag / version | `etag a -> b, version v1 -> v2` |
| `git` | files | `git diff --name-status` + `--numstat` | `modified main.py +1 -1` |
| `icechunk` | nodes | `Repository.diff(from, to)` | `modified /x 2 chunks` |
| `iceberg` | snapshots | snapshot summaries along `b`'s ancestry to `a` | `append: +5 rows, +1 files` |
| `delta` | commits | transaction-log `history()` in `(a, b]` | `WRITE: +2 rows, +1 files` |
| `lance` | fragments | fragment ids / deletions / schema at both versions | `added fragment 1 +1 rows` |
| `ducklake` | tables | snapshot `changes` + `ducklake_table_changes` | `modified main.t +5000 rows, -1 rows` |
| `dolt` | tables | `dolt_diff_summary` + `dolt_diff_stat` | `modified t +6 rows` |
| `neon` | -- | no native diff | |

A directory or prefix state is only a digest, so it cannot be diffed on its
own. At commit time the `file` backend hands the engine a per-file listing; it
is stored content-addressed under `.tether/listings/` and committed with the
manifests (the same trick as DVC's `.dir` files). `diff --content` compares
two listings file by file; diffs of commits made before listings existed fall
back to a count/size summary. `gc` removes listings no manifest references.
Entries are capped at 2000 per object; counts are exact.

## `file`: local paths and object stores

Plain artifacts: a local file or directory, or an object / prefix in S3
(`s3://`), GCS (`gs://`), or Azure Blob (`az://`, `abfs://`), through
[obstore](https://developmentseed.org/obstore/).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional; `path` accepted). A trailing `/` (or empty key) means a prefix. `region` overrides the store region. |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `obstore.store.from_url`. Committed (`tether.toml`): only the allowlisted `region`, `allow_http`, `virtual_hosted_style_request`, `conditional_put`; endpoints, account names, and credentials only in `.tether/secrets.toml`, which may also name a `profile`/`role_arn` or literal keys per URI prefix or object. Otherwise credentials come from the environment / instance metadata. |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | local file: `type=file, size, sha256`; local dir: `type=dir, count, size, digest` (digest over per-file sha256s); remote object: `type=object, size, etag[, version_id]`; prefix: `type=prefix, count, size, digest` (one paged `LIST`, etag+size per key). Local hashes are cached by `(size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, inode)` in `.tether/cache/file-hashes.json`, so only files whose stat changed are re-read |
| Tier | Observed by default. `--file versioned` on a single *remote* object makes it Addressable via `version_id` (S3 version id / GCS generation / Azure version id; requires versioning on the bucket/container -- a recorded state without a version id is refused by `open`). Local paths and prefixes are always Observed. |
| Pin / fork | none |
| Handle | `FileHandle(uri, version_id)` -- always read-only |
| Listing | directories and prefixes hand the engine a per-file JSONL listing (`{"p": path, "k": token, "s": size}`) that is stored under `.tether/listings/` |
| Diff | `files`: per-path added/removed/modified with size deltas from two stored listings; falls back to a count/size summary when a listing is missing; single objects report changed size/etag/sha256/version |
| Create | a local directory only (`mkdir` plus a `.tether-owner` marker file the directory walk skips, so the directory fingerprints as empty until something is written). Ref-empty means nothing but the marker; `delete_store` is an `rmdir` that refuses anything else. Remote prefixes are not created or removed by tether. |
| Notes | `--file immutable` (default) turns any drift into an `ImmutableObjectModified` error at `status` -- and drift means the *bytes* changed, not the timestamp. Local walks use `os.scandir`. A symlink to a file is read through; a symlink to a directory, or a dangling one, is recorded by its target, so retargeting it is a change but edits under a linked directory are not seen. The first fingerprint of a large tree reads every file (sha256 at ~1.5-3 GB/s per core, up to 8 files at a time); later ones read only what changed, except files changed within two seconds of the last read, which are read again. |

## `icechunk`: Icechunk repositories

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (local path or `s3://bucket/prefix`), `branch` (default `main`), `region` (S3) |
| Config | none committed. `.tether/secrets.toml` may set `profile`, `role_arn`, literal keys, `endpoint_url`, `region` per URI prefix or object, so two repositories in two accounts pin in one `commit` (see [Configuration](08-configuration.qmd#advanced-two-stores-two-identities)); otherwise S3 credentials come from the environment (`from_env`). For an S3-compatible server (SeaweedFS, MinIO) the same entry sets `allow_http = true` (plain HTTP to `endpoint_url`) and `force_path_style = true` (the bucket in the path); both reach every Icechunk and obstore call, `add --create` and `delete_store` included. |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `snapshot_id` of the branch head |
| Pin | `create_tag("tether.<id>", snapshot_id)`; tags are immutable, and the default `expire_snapshots` keeps a tagged snapshot. `expire_snapshots(delete_expired_tags=True)` deletes the tag and the snapshot with it; `verify` then reports the pin `missing` |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, snapshot_id)` off the tag (`reset_branch` if it exists) |
| Handle | `IcechunkHandle(repository, session, branch, tag, snapshot_id)`; `session` is writable for a branch, read-only for a tag/snapshot |
| Diff | `nodes`: `Repository.diff(from, to)` -- new/deleted groups and arrays, updated metadata, updated chunk counts per array, moves |
| Create | `Repository.create`, refused if anything exists at the path or under the prefix (not only a repository); the owner marker is the `tether.owner` key in the repository's metadata (needs an icechunk with `Repository.exists` and repository metadata -- 2.2.0 is known to work; older ones lose the `CREATE` capability with a clear error). Ref-empty: no branch but the base, no tag (a pin's later generation `tether.<id>.N` counts as the pin the plan names), and the base still at the repository's first snapshot. `delete_store` re-checks owner and emptiness, then removes only Icechunk's own top-level names (1.x and 2.x layouts) -- a directory or prefix holding anything else is refused and kept. |

## `neon`: Neon Postgres

*Experimental*: tested against a fake of the Neon API, not a live project.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `project_id`, `database`, `role` (all required: Neon builds no connection URI without a database and a role, so `add` refuses a locator missing one), `branch` (default `main`) |
| Config | `api_key_env` (default `NEON_API_KEY`), `api_url` (default Neon API v2), `protected_pins` (default `false`; `true` creates each pin as a protected branch, which Neon refuses to delete -- Free has none and paid plans allow a few, and every commit that pins makes one) -- `.tether/secrets.toml` only; a committed value is refused |
| Identity | `{project_id, branch}` -- a Neon branch at an LSN is a snapshot of the whole project, so `database` and `role` are how you connect, not what you pin: neither changes pin ids, and two objects on two databases of one project share one pin per commit and (via `branch_scope`) one working branch per bookmark |
| State | `lsn`, `commit_xid`, `branch`, `timeline` (probed over SQL on the working or source branch). Content is `commit_xid` and `branch`, the *lineage*: the object's source branch when the branch read descends from it, so an untouched fork compares equal to its pin. `lsn` (it advances on checkpoints) and `timeline` (the branch the LSN was actually read on) are volatile address keys. `commit_xid` is the newest *committed* transaction id: a compute restart moves the next id past ids no transaction used, which does not count as a write. With no commit among the last 65536 ids it reads `<N` (the next id), so a later commit still shows as a change |
| Pin | a child branch `tether.<id>` of the state's timeline at its LSN (so a fork's pin hangs off the fork, not `main`), protected only with `protected_pins = true`; `RETENTION_BOUND` by the project's history retention |
| Fork | a child branch of the pin. Re-forking an existing working branch restores it onto the source (Neon branch restore, always -- a branch's `parent_id` says where it was created, not where its head is). Once a pin has been taken on the working branch that pin is its child and Neon will not restore it in place, so the fork lands on a sibling (`<name>.2`, `.3`, ...) and the old branch stays as the pins' parent; the engine records the returned name. A branch tether reads or writes gets a `read_write` endpoint on first use (a fingerprint, the quiescence check, `open`); pins and time-travel reads (`open` at a recorded state) get a `read_only` one. Every connection URI names the endpoint it is for |
| Quiescence | `commit` refuses while `pg_stat_activity` shows active writers (`--force` skips) |
| Handle | `NeonHandle(url, branch)` -- a Postgres connection URL |
| Diff | not supported (no native primitive) |
| Notes | pins are branches, and branches are the storage: what that means for `gc`, `new`, `promote`, cost, and fingerprinting is in one place, [Caveats: Neon](12-caveats-and-performance.qmd#neon). |

## `git`: git and jj repositories

Pin the *code* (or any git-tracked data) that produced a dataset. Colocated
jj repositories work through their `.git`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `path` (local checkout, stored absolute, and outside the dataset's own checkout; the positional locator works too: `tether add code --kind git ../code`), `ref` (default `HEAD`), `remote` (push pins there: the name of a remote the repository has configured; a URL or path only as `[objects."<key>"] remote` in `.tether/secrets.toml`), `allow_dirty` (pin despite uncommitted changes) |
| Config | `git_path`, `jj_path` -- `.tether/secrets.toml` `[vcs]` or `TETHER_GIT`/`TETHER_JJ` only; a committed value is refused |
| Identity | `{path}` (resolved absolute) |
| State | `sha`; `dirty` (only meaningful -- and only computed -- for the checked-out ref); `change_id` when jj is available. Both `dirty` and `change_id` are volatile: the same sha is the same state -- and pins identically -- whether or not jj is installed or the checkout has stray files; `pin` still reads the full state and refuses a dirty tree |
| Pin | lightweight tag `tether.<id>` at the sha. With `remote` set the pin is pushed and is only a pin once the push succeeds: a failed push fails the `pin` and removes the local tag; `unpin` deletes on the remote first and fails if that fails, so local and remote never diverge silently |
| Fork | branch `name` at the tag's sha (`branch -f` if it exists) |
| Handle | `GitHandle(path, sha, worktree)` |
| Diff | `files`: `git diff --name-status -M` with `--numstat` line counts (`+a -d`) |
| Create | `git init -b <ref>` plus one empty root commit with a fixed tree, author, and dates, so every store tether creates has the same root sha (`GitBackend.EMPTY_ROOT_SHA`) and the base branch exists to pin and fork from; the owner marker is `git config tether.owner`. Ref-empty: no branch or tag beyond the base, the base *at* that root sha (an amended root is not), and a clean working tree (`git status --porcelain --ignored`: an untracked, staged, or ignored file is data `delete_store` would take with the directory). `delete_store` re-checks both and removes the repository directory only then. |
| Notes | remote-only (url) repositories are not supported yet. Every git call runs with `core.fsmonitor`, hooks, and `ext::` transports off and `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, so a repository's config runs nothing. `promote` and `merge` move a branch: with the default `ref = HEAD` that is the checked-out branch, and a detached `HEAD` -- a colocated jj checkout always has one -- is refused; set `ref` to the branch name to promote there. |

## `iceberg`: Apache Iceberg tables

*Experimental*: driven through a fake of the pyiceberg table API; not yet run
against a catalog service.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `identifier` (`ns.table`; `table` accepted), `branch` (default `main`), `catalog_name` (default `default`), `catalog` (dict of pyiceberg catalog properties, or set once in config) |
| Config | `catalog = {...}` pyiceberg properties. Committed (`tether.toml` or the locator): exactly `type`, `warehouse` and `name`; every other property -- `uri`, `token`, `credential`, ... -- only in `.tether/secrets.toml` (`[backends.iceberg] catalog` or per identifier) |
| Identity | `{identifier, branch, catalog_name}` |
| State | `snapshot_id` (nothing else: `metadata_location` changes on every table commit on any branch). A new table with no snapshot yet has `snapshot_id = -1`, Iceberg's "no current snapshot" |
| Pin | `--pin native` (default): tag `tether.<id>`; `--pin record`: no native ref, the snapshot id alone (drops `PIN`; recoverable only within snapshot retention -- for S3 Tables and other catalogs where user refs disable maintenance). The empty state needs no tag: its pin verifies as held and opens at `snapshot_id = -1`, which pyiceberg's scans refuse rather than read today's data |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, snapshot_id)`; re-forking an existing name re-points it (a `set-snapshot-ref` update). A table with no snapshot cannot be forked -- pyiceberg writes no branch before the first snapshot -- so write it on the trunk bookmark first. Needs pyiceberg 0.11 or newer (`promote` onto `main` uses `set_current_snapshot`) |
| Handle | `IcebergHandle(table, ref, snapshot_id)` |
| Diff | `snapshots`: one entry per snapshot on `b`'s ancestry back to `a`, from snapshot summaries (`append: +5 rows, +1 files`); when `a` is not an ancestor, `total-*` counters are compared instead |

## `delta`: Delta Lake tables

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional), `region` (sets `AWS_REGION`) |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `DeltaTable`. Committed: only `region`, `allow_http`, `virtual_hosted_style_request`, `conditional_put`; endpoints and credentials in `.tether/secrets.toml` (per URI prefix or object) |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `version`, `table_id` (metadata id -- a recreated table verifies as drifted) |
| Pin / fork | none: Delta has no tags or branches. Versions stay readable until `VACUUM` (7-day default) / log retention (30 days). |
| Handle | `DeltaHandle(uri, version, table)` -- read-only `DeltaTable` at the version |
| Diff | `commits`: one entry per transaction-log commit in `(a, b]` with its operation and metrics (`WRITE: +2 rows, +1 files`) |

## `lance`: Lance datasets

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `uri` (positional), `branch` (default `main`) |
| Config | `storage_options = {...}` passed to `lance.dataset`. Committed: only `region`, `allow_http`, `virtual_hosted_style_request`, `conditional_put`; endpoints and credentials in `.tether/secrets.toml` (per URI prefix or object) |
| Identity | `{uri}` |
| State | `branch`, `version`, and on any branch but `main` its `branch_id` (Lance version numbers are branch-scoped and restart when a branch is deleted and re-created, so the id tells two lives of one name apart; `--at N` means version `N` of the locator's `branch` -- it is a *base* coordinate and is never consulted once a working branch exists; use a tag to name a version on another branch) |
| Pin | `tags.create("tether.<id>", (branch, version))`; tagged versions are exempt from `cleanup_old_versions()` |
| Fork | `create_branch(name, tag)`. Lance refuses to delete a branch a tag references, so a pinned working branch outlives its workspace and a re-fork under the same name picks `name.2`, `name.3`, ... |
| Handle | `LanceHandle(uri, dataset, version, branch, tag)`; append with `lance.write_dataset(table, handle.dataset, mode="append")` |
| Diff | `fragments`: fragment ids added/removed, deletion-file changes, columns added/removed, from the two manifests |
| Notes | an untouched fork reports its parent's `(branch, version)`, so a no-op commit after `tether new` is a no-op. |

## `ducklake`: DuckLake catalogs

*Experimental*: tested against a local DuckDB-file catalog, not a Postgres or
MySQL catalog with an object-store `data_path`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `metadata` (positional `uri` accepted; the `ducklake:` prefix is added if missing, e.g. `ducklake:postgres:dbname=lake`; a relative DuckDB or SQLite file path in it is stored absolute, as `data_path` is), `data_path`, `table` (scopes the handle only -- snapshots are catalog-wide) |
| Config | `init_sql = ["CREATE SECRET ...", ...]` run on every fresh connection -- `.tether/secrets.toml` only (it runs code); credentials there or in the environment, never in the locator |
| Identity | `{metadata[, data_path]}` |
| State | `snapshot_id`, `snapshot_time_us` (epoch microseconds; a recreated catalog verifies as drifted) |
| Pin / fork | none: DuckLake has no tags or branches. `ducklake_expire_snapshots` bounds how long a snapshot stays readable. |
| Handle | `DuckLakeHandle(metadata, alias, connection, snapshot_id, attach_sql, data_path, table)`: a DuckDB connection with the catalog attached read-only (at `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` for a recorded state); `table_ref()` gives `alias.table`; `close()` / `with handle:` detaches |
| Diff | `tables`: per-table created/dropped/altered/inserted/deleted from the snapshots' `changes` maps, with row counts from `ducklake_table_changes` for tables that still exist |
| Notes | a DuckDB-file metadata catalog can be attached only once per process: operations attach/detach per call (serialized per catalog), and an open handle or your own writer connection in the same process blocks `status`. Postgres/SQLite/MySQL catalogs have no such limit. |

## `dolt`: Dolt databases

*Experimental*: tested against a fake of the Dolt SQL surface, not a running
`dolt sql-server`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Locator | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default 3306), `database` (required), `branch` (default `main`), `user`; or `url = mysql://user@host:port/database` |
| Credentials | the server's `[uris."mysql://host:port"]` entry in `.tether/secrets.toml` (a `mysql://host:port/database` entry beats it): `user` and `password`, or `user_env` and `password_env` naming environment variables. Only those entries: an `[objects."<key>"]` entry, the `[backends.dolt]` section and the environment by convention are ignored. A manifest chooses the host, so a server with no entry gets no password (and user `root` unless the locator names one) |
| Identity | `{host, port, database}` |
| State | `commit` (branch head hash), plus `dirty = true` when `dolt_branches.dirty` reports uncommitted working-set changes (refused at pin time) |
| Pin | `CALL DOLT_TAG('tether.<id>', commit)` |
| Fork | `CALL DOLT_BRANCH(name, tag)` (recreated with `-D` if it exists at another commit) |
| Promote / merge | `DOLT_MERGE` (`--ff-only` to promote) inside an explicit transaction: under autocommit Dolt rolls a conflicting merge back with an error, so only a transaction can report which tables conflict or violate a constraint. Those come back as `MergeConflict`, and the merge is aborted and rolled back |
| Handle | `DoltHandle(url, database, ref, commit)`: a revision-database URL `mysql://user@host:port/db/<branch|tag|hash>` (tags and hashes are read-only in Dolt); `database_ref` is `db/ref` for `USE` |
| Diff | `tables`: `dolt_diff_summary` (added/dropped/modified/renamed tables, schema changes) with `dolt_diff_stat` row counts |
| Notes | talks to `dolt sql-server` / Hosted Dolt via PyMySQL; the SQL surface sits behind the `DoltClient` protocol (`tether.experimental.backends.dolt`) so other transports can be substituted. |

## `memory`: in-process reference backend

The executable specification of the protocol, used by the conformance suite and
the engine tests. Locator `{system, branch}`; state `snapshot_id`; tags and
branches in a process-global `MemoryStore` (`tether.backends.memory.default_store()`).
`MemoryHandle.read()` / `.write(payload)` operate on the current ref; `diff`
reports changed payload keys.
